stops.note: 'part'; Caesar's Gallic War opens 'Gallia est omnis divisa in partes tres', Gaul is divided into three parts
from partir 'to divide'; a part, a side in a quarrel, or a litigant in court, the sense still used in legal 'third party'
the political sense grew with the Whigs and Tories of the 1680s; a 'party' as a social gathering dates from the 1700s

current_meaning: a social gathering; a political organisation; a person or group in an agreement
